Disable execution of multiple statements in a single SQL query
issue_title: Prevent SQL injections by locking PDO to single statements
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing features request](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AImprovement%2CFeature%2CDeveloper+Feature+) and found no previous suggestion of this feature.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

For legacy reasons, SQL queries in PrestaShop are not handled via [prepared statements](https://www.php.net/manual/en/pdo.prepare.php) using named arguments, and instead they are made using string interpolation. This is how we can got SQL injection vulnerabilities, like the one that was fixed recently in the Wishlist module.

### Describe the solution you'd like

By [disabling multiple queries](https://www.php.net/manual/en/ref.pdo-mysql.php#pdo.constants.mysql-attr-multi-statements) in the PDO connection's configuration, we could mitigate the risk of data manipulation via SQL injection, because sequential queries won't be executed.


### Alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Do you plan to work on this feature?

- [ ] I'm willing to contribute a [formal specification](https://github.com/PrestaShop/prestashop-specs).
- [ ] I'm willing to provide any wireframes or design assets required for this feature.
- [ ] I'm willing to submit a Pull Request that implements this feature.
- [ ] I'm willing to help verify that the implemented feature works as intended and produces no unintended side effects.

title: Upgrade shivammathur/setup_php in github actions
issue_title: Workflows are referencing vulnerable actions
issue_body:
Hello, there! 

As part of the university research we are currently doing regarding the security of Github Actions, we noticed that one or many of the workflows that are part of this repository are referencing vulnerable versions of the third-party actions. As part of a disclosure process, we decided to open issues to notify GitHub Community. 

*Please note that there are could be some false positives in our methodology, thus not all of the open issues could be valid. If that is the case, please let us know, so that we can improve on our approach. You can contact me directly using an email: ikoishy [at] ncsu.edu* 

Thanks in advance
1. The workflow **cron_js_routing.yml** is referencing action **shivammathur/setup-php** using references **v1**. However this reference is missing the commit [7163319](https://github.com/shivammathur/setup-php/commits/7163319) which may contain fix to the vulnerability.
1. The workflow **cron_nightly.yml** is referencing action **shivammathur/setup-php** using references **v1**. However this reference is missing the commit [7163319](https://github.com/shivammathur/setup-php/commits/7163319) which may contain fix to the vulnerability.

The vulnerability fix that is missing by actions' versions could be related to: 
(1) CVE fix 
(2) upgrade of vulnerable dependency 
(3) fix to secret leak and others. 
Please consider updating the reference to the action. 

*If you end up updating the reference, please let us know. We need the stats for the paper :-)*

issue_body:
Currently, when multistore is enabled, the product page is disabled in group shop context.

In the new experimental product page, multistore has not been tested yet, we don't know if it works properly even in all shop and single shop context.

So with @jolelievre we thought it would be a good idea to block the page and display a message if there is more than one shop enabled, until we make this page thoroughly multistore compatible.

@MatShir what do you think ?

Solution:

Display the following message:
'Note that this page is available in a single shop context only. Switch context to work on it.' in Admin.Notifications.Info

title: Remove inline-style from form_row of the UIKit and adapt js
issue_title: Invalid inline style in PrestaShop UI Kit symfony form theme
issue_body:
<!--
****************************
DO NOT disclose security issues here, contact security@prestashop.com instead!
****************************
-->

#### Describe the bug

In the prestashop UI kit form theme some inline code has been added in. the `form_row` block:

```twig
    <div class="{{ block('form_row_class') }}{{ block('widget_type_class') }}{% if (not compound or force_error|default(false)) and not valid %} has-error{% endif %}"{% if (attr.visible is defined and not attr.visible) %} style="display: none;"{% endif %}>
```

This part in particular `{% if (attr.visible is defined and not attr.visible) %} style="display: none;"{% endif %}` we should use a class instead (like `d-none`) This option seems to be only used in `PrestaShopBundle\Form\Admin\Sell\Address\CustomerAddressType` (strangely not in the other address types).

This should be fixed in the theme, but maybe also in the js of the customer address (if we use a class the js might just use `.show()/.hide()` and it won't work any more).

#### Expected behavior

Same behaviour but with clean theme without hard coded inline style.

**Screenshots**

If applicable, add screenshots or screen recordings to help explain your problem.

#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: 1.7.8
* PHP version: N/A

title: Improve accessibility of classic theme forms by adding for and ids
issue_title: [Accessibility] Default theme: form fields not associated to their label make them impossible to fill for blind users
issue_body:
#### Describe the bug

A lot of forms in the default Prestashop theme have form fields not associated to their label so it's making them impossible to fill for blind users. **It's a huge accessibility problem.**

As a result, a lot of Prestashop shops do not have accessible forms because the default theme is a model for developers…

#### Expected behavior

Associate form fields to their label. It's a basic HTML feature where you need to have a `for` attribute on `label` elements and an `id` attribute on form fields (`input`, `textarea`, `select`). The value of the `for` attribute must be the value of its field `id`. IDs must be unique in a page, of course, so that it can work.

Example:

```html
<label for="username">Username</label>
<input id="username" type="text" name="username">
```

[See the WAI doc here](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tips/developing/#associate-a-label-with-every-form-control)

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Go on the demo site: https://demo.prestashop.com/#/en/front
2. Go on create account page or sign in, or add products to cart and go to checkout: guest checkout or sign in forms, etc.
3. Open the browser development tools and see that there is no `for` attribute on `label` elements nor `id` attribute on form fields. A screen reader, tool used by blind people to navigate in their computer, will not be able to tell what value the field is expecting.

#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: N/A
* PHP version: N/A
